task: Read-only source inventory for original Pokémon Mystery Dungeon Red/Blue Rescue Team; implementation recommendations are design judgments, not claims of emulation fidelity.
sourceUseNote: Game facts use original-generation sections of Bulbapedia. Technical facts use project documentation, MDN, W3C, and GitHub Docs. Ref IDs are included so the parent can open the sources before citing them.

roster.mainFactSummary: All species from Generations I–III are obtainable. Original level-up learnsets derive from FireRed/LeafGreen. Use a 386-species registry; forms and story actors need separate identities.
roster.partnerRule: Original partner choice excludes the hero's type.

versionDifferences.caveat: The main game page's blue table omits Porygon2 but explicitly identifies it as a wild Blue exclusive below the table. Upgrade exists in both versions. Wonder Mail can unlock opposite-version species. Do not model these as permanently unobtainable.

exceptions.name: Munchlax
exceptions.status: NPC cameo; not recruitable in the originals

exceptions.name: Unown
exceptions.status: Model forms separately from species; each form can be recruited and appears separately in recruitment search.

exceptions.name: Deoxys
exceptions.status: One species with four forms; in the originals it is Normal outside dungeons and randomly changes form on each new floor. Form effects use stat-stage changes.

capacityCaveat.text: 413 is recruited-Pokémon capacity, not the number of species.

recommendations: Use stable numeric species IDs plus independent form IDs, entity IDs and recruit IDs.
If the brief requires every original Pokémon, all 386 must have an actual route to recruitment or evolution and functional moves; a searchable encyclopedia alone does not satisfy that requirement.
Keep original starter restrictions as a Classic option if offering free character selection; describe free selection as an intentional change.
Do not introduce Fairy typing, Mega Evolution, later cross-generation evolutions, or DX-only recruitment mechanics.

dungeonInventory.countingConvention: 45 named traversable field dungeons, counting Rock Path and Snow Path and the four Wonder Mail dungeons, but grouping summit/pit/grotto sections under their parent dungeons. Separate Dojo and wireless feature below.
dungeonInventory.multiPartNote: A completeness manifest should track these as dungeon segments with their own floor/boss metadata, rather than silently dropping them or double-counting them as independent field dungeons.

dojo.note: Standard mazes are three floors. Rescue Team Maze uses a team transferred from Red through the DS GBA slot; browser adaptation needs an explicit import or authored substitute.

unknownDungeon.note: Not a manually explored dungeon. Include as a documented adaptation or feature entry instead of claiming a missing map.

completenessPitfalls: Many Bulbapedia pages mix original Generation III and Rescue Team DX Generation VIII tables. Copy only original tables and explicit RB flags.
A count such as 43 often omits the two fugitive paths. State the counting convention.
A name-only dungeon list does not establish exact encounter tables, floor counts, item pools, weather, traps, level-reset conditions, unlocks or boss behavior. Those still need source-specific data.
Field floors, fixed boss arenas, rest areas and summit sections need separate metadata.
Dojo type list is 17 in the originals; do not add the DX Fairy Maze.

recommendedStructuredBase.scope: Species identity, names, original type history, versioned learnsets, main-series base stats, evolution facts.
recommendedStructuredBase.fileNamesCaveat: Names describe the expected current CSV tables; inspect the pinned repository directory before scripting, especially historical-stat tables whose schema changed recently.
recommendedStructuredBase.filter: Species generation_id <= 3 or National IDs 1..386; resolve original forms explicitly; level-up moves filtered to version group firered-leafgreen.
recommendedStructuredBase.historyRule: API past_types, past_abilities and past_stats record values valid through the listed generation. Apply the correct history interval instead of taking present-day fields.
recommendedStructuredBase.license: Repository is BSD-3-Clause. Retain the exact copyright, conditions and disclaimer from its pinned LICENSE.md in the embedded credits/source notice. Names remain Pokémon/Nintendo trademarks.

criticalFidelityBoundary.statement: PokéAPI identifies its provenance as main-series data. Its base stats, move damage, PP, accuracy, ranges and encounter data must not be labeled original PMD values.
criticalFidelityBoundary.recommendation: Keep PMD stats and move effects in a separate authored data layer. If adapting formulas for a new browser roguelike, describe them as adapted rather than exact original mechanics.

pmdSpecificReference.observed: The decompilation build references monster/monster_data.json and monster/learnset/learnset_data.json, plus dungeon, item and move data build files.
pmdSpecificReference.caveat: No permissive license was established for this decompilation. Do not assume open visibility permits wholesale redistribution of game code, art, dialogue or audio.
pmdSpecificReference.recommendation: Use documented factual references and independently implement behavior; do not embed ROM data or copied original scripts/assets as a shortcut.

dataAvailability.attributionRecommendation: Embed a Credits and Sources panel with factual-reference URLs, research date, data edition, three.js MIT notice and PokéAPI license. Use original procedural graphics and authored short narrative text. Avoid importing Bulbapedia prose wholesale.
requiredDataAudits: No species IDs outside 1..386 in recruit registry
Every species has at least one obtainability route
No Fairy type in original rules
Every dungeon ID resolves to floors and an unlock route
No later-generation moves from unfiltered API records
Forms remain distinct from species count
Original PMD numerical values are sourced separately from main-series values

staticWebGLArchitecture.recommendation: Embed a pinned, build-time bundled Three.js engine and all application code/data directly in one HTML file. No import from a CDN, runtime fetch, external font, texture URL, model URL or audio URL.

technicalFacts.text: Current Three.js WebGLRenderer uses WebGL2; WebGL1 support ended at r163.
Three.js uses the MIT license and requires preservation of its notice.
GitHub Pages serves static HTML, CSS and JavaScript from a repository.

implementationJudgments: Use one bundled IIFE or one dependency-free inline module. Eliminate dynamic imports and URL-resolved assets. Preserve exact pinned engine version and license.
Bundle before inserting into HTML; escape case-insensitive closing script sequences in embedded strings and JSON. Do not paste a modern three.module.js file with unresolved imports.
Keep deterministic turn simulation independent of rendering. Rendering interpolates completed actions and never advances hunger, AI, damage or RNG by elapsed frame time.

Use an orthographic or shallow-perspective isometric camera with real meshes, fog, materials and lighting; procedural species silhouettes need identifiable features per species rather than color-swapped generic blobs.
Use shared geometry/materials and instancing for floor/wall/decor batches. Seed terrain decoration separately from gameplay RNG. Dispose geometry and textures when unloading a floor.
Build tiny canvas textures at startup if necessary; those become local GPU textures without a network request. Use synthesized Web Audio for optional effects after a user gesture.

Render the visible floor neighborhood with a controlled draw-call budget. Cap effective pixel ratio around 1.5–2 and expose a low-effects setting. Avoid expensive full-scene shadow maps, heavy transparency and postprocessing on mobile.
Use requestAnimationFrame only for active animation, pause decorative rendering while hidden, and retain a single WebGL canvas/context.
Catch renderer creation failure and context loss. Present a usable textual status, save/export controls and explicit recovery action; do not leave a blank screen.
Embed original gameplay constants and provenance metadata in application/json. Treat save/import files as untrusted structured data with size/type/range validation.

performanceBasis.summary: MDN recommends bounded VRAM, smaller back buffers, resource deletion and batching. The proposed numeric rendering budget and camera/art design are engineering judgments.

saveDesign.facts: localStorage is scoped to origin, may be blocked, and has undefined behavior for file URLs.
recommendations: Use a namespaced schema-versioned save key and catch read/write errors.
Save only serializable simulation state, RNG state and progression; reconstruct render resources.
Keep two rotating checkpoints or last-valid save.
Offer JSON export/import so a self-contained downloaded HTML remains usable without reliable localStorage.
Never call localStorage.clear(); only touch this application's keys.

standards.text: WCAG 2.2 AA target-size minimum is 24 CSS pixels, subject to exceptions.

recommendations: Make primary touch controls at least 44–48 CSS pixels as a comfort target.
Use Pointer Events and separate taps for move/wait/attack; support diagonal movement with an explicit diagonal mode or clear 8-direction pad.
Provide keyboard equivalents, visible focus, semantic HTML buttons, accessible names and Escape/back actions.
Prevent page scrolling only for relevant focused gameplay keys; do not trap Tab or browser shortcuts.
Put HP, belly, floor, selected move, inventory and combat log in DOM text as well as graphics.
Use a restrained live region for meaningful turn events; avoid announcing every decorative frame.
Make turn-based planning available without animation deadlines; reduced-motion mode skips camera shake, flashes and long transitions.
Do not convey type, status, interactability or damage solely by color.
Keep controls and menus usable in portrait and landscape with safe-area insets and dynamic viewport height.
Support browser zoom and text resize; do not use user-scalable=no.
